name: Financial Compliance Agent
description: An AI agent designed for compliance officers to analyze regulatory adherence, counterparty risk, and risk event history in financial institutions.
system_prompt:
You are RegulatoryRisk GraphAgent, an expert financial compliance advisor with deep knowledge of Basel IV, Basel III, DORA, Dodd-Frank, and SREP regulations. You have access to a knowledge graph of financial institutions, their regulatory obligations, implemented controls, counterparty exposures, and historical risk events.

When answering questions:
- Always cite the specific graph relationships you traversed to reach your answer
- Explain WHY something is compliant or non-compliant, not just whether it is
- For counterparty risk, always quantify the exposure in USD and number of hops
- For missing controls, always state which specific rule requires that control
- For risk events, always connect them to the rule that was violated
- Never give a one-line answer — always explain the compliance reasoning behind it

Tool priority: Use Cypher Template tools first. Use Similarity Search for incident matching. Use Text2Cypher only as absolute last resort for simple aggregations.

tools.name: Missing Regulatory Controls for Bank
tools.description: Identifies which regulatory controls a specific bank is currently missing based on applicable regulations.

config.template:
MATCH (e:Entity {name: $bank_name})
MATCH (e)-[:SUBJECT_TO]->(:Regulation)-[:CONTAINS]->(:Rule)-[:REQUIRES_CONTROL]->(requiredControl:Control)
WHERE NOT EXISTS {
  (e)-[:IMPLEMENTS]->(requiredControl)
}
RETURN DISTINCT requiredControl.name AS MissingControl, requiredControl.description AS ControlDescription, requiredControl.category AS Category
ORDER BY requiredControl.name

parameters.name: bank_name
parameters.description: The exact name of the financial institution (Entity).

tools.name: Counterparty Contagion Paths
tools.description: Finds potential multi-hop counterparty contagion risk paths between two specified banks, showing the path and aggregated exposure.

config.template:
MATCH p=(startBank:Entity {name: $start_bank})-[:COUNTERPARTY_OF*1..3]-(endBank:Entity)
RETURN
  [node IN NODES(p) | node.name] AS Path,
  REDUCE(totalExposure = 0, rel IN RELATIONSHIPS(p) | totalExposure + rel.exposure_usd) AS TotalExposureUSD,
  LENGTH(p) AS Hops,
  endBank.name AS ConnectedBank,
  endBank.country AS Country
ORDER BY TotalExposureUSD DESC, Hops ASC
LIMIT 10

parameters.name: start_bank
parameters.description: The exact name of the starting financial institution (Entity).

tools.name: Rules Violated by Risk Event
tools.description: Retrieves the rules that were triggered or violated by a specific risk event.

config.template:
MATCH (e:Entity)-[:INVOLVED_IN]->(re:RiskEvent {id: $risk_event_id})-[:TRIGGERED_BY]->(rule:Rule)<-[:CONTAINS]-(reg:Regulation)
RETURN 
  re.type AS EventType,
  re.severity AS Severity,
  re.date AS EventDate,
  re.description AS EventDescription,
  e.name AS EntityInvolved,
  rule.id AS RuleID,
  rule.section AS RuleSection,
  rule.text AS RuleText,
  reg.name AS Regulation
ORDER BY rule.id

parameters.name: risk_event_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the RiskEvent.

tools.name: Bank Regulations and Enforcement
tools.description: Lists the regulations a bank is subject to and details about the enforcing regulator, if available.

config.template:
MATCH (bank:Entity {name: $bank_name})-[st:SUBJECT_TO]->(reg:Regulation)
OPTIONAL MATCH (reg)-[:ENFORCED_BY]->(regulator:Regulator)
RETURN
    reg.name AS RegulationName,
    reg.description AS Description,
    reg.jurisdiction AS Jurisdiction,
    reg.effective_date AS EffectiveDate,
    regulator.name AS EnforcedByRegulator,
    regulator.authority_level AS RegulatorAuthorityLevel,
    st.since_date AS SubjectToSince
ORDER BY RegulationName

parameters.name: bank_name
parameters.description: The exact name of the financial institution (Entity).

tools.name: Superseding Basel Rules
tools.description: Traces which 'Basel IV' rules supersede older 'Basel III' rules.

config.template:
MATCH (newRule:Rule)-[:SUPERSEDES]->(oldRule:Rule)
MATCH (newReg:Regulation)-[:CONTAINS]->(newRule)
MATCH (oldReg:Regulation)-[:CONTAINS]->(oldRule)
RETURN
  newReg.name AS NewRegulation,
  newRule.id AS NewRuleID,
  newRule.section AS NewRuleSection,
  newRule.text AS NewRuleText,
  oldReg.name AS SupersedesRegulation,
  oldRule.id AS OldRuleID,
  oldRule.section AS OldRuleSection,
  oldRule.text AS OldRuleText
ORDER BY newRule.id

tools.name: Search Similar Risk Events
tools.description: Given a description of a risk incident, finds the most semantically similar past risk events from the knowledge graph. Use this tool when the user describes a new incident or asks about similar historical events, breaches, or violations.

tools.name: Natural Language to Cypher Tool
tools.description: Last resort fallback tool only. Use this tool ONLY when none of the other specialized tools (Missing Regulatory Controls, Counterparty Contagion Paths, Rules Violated by Risk Event, Bank Regulations and Enforcement, Superseding Basel Rules, Search Similar Risk Events) can answer the question. Suitable for ad-hoc aggregation queries such as counting entities, listing all regulations, or summarizing statistics across the graph.

tools.name: Preventive Controls for Risk Event
tools.description: Given a risk event ID, finds the controls that would have prevented it by traversing from the triggered rule to its required controls, and checks which of those controls the involved entity had implemented at the time.

config.template:
MATCH (e:Entity)-[:INVOLVED_IN]->(re:RiskEvent {id: $risk_event_id})-[:TRIGGERED_BY]->(rule:Rule)-[:REQUIRES_CONTROL]->(ctrl:Control)
OPTIONAL MATCH (e)-[impl:IMPLEMENTS]->(ctrl)
RETURN
  re.id AS EventID,
  re.type AS EventType,
  e.name AS EntityInvolved,
  rule.section AS ViolatedRule,
  ctrl.name AS RequiredControl,
  ctrl.category AS ControlCategory,
  ctrl.description AS ControlDescription,
  CASE WHEN impl IS NULL THEN 'NOT IMPLEMENTED' ELSE impl.status END AS ImplementationStatus,
  CASE WHEN impl IS NULL THEN 'This control was missing and would have prevented the event'
  ELSE 'Control existed but may have been insufficient' END AS Assessment
ORDER BY ctrl.category

parameters.name: risk_event_id
parameters.description: The ID of the risk event e.g. EVT-001
